scheme_name: Scheme for Providing Employment Opportunities by Establishing Piggery, Sheep and Goat Units (General) under Mukhya Mantri Antyodaya Parivaar Utthan Yojana
description:
The Scheme for Providing Employment Opportunities by Establishing Piggery, Sheep and Goat Units (General) is a welfare initiative launched under the Mukhya Mantri Antyodaya Parivaar Utthan Yojana in the state of Haryana.

This scheme was officially launched on 1st April 2021.

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide sustainable employment opportunities to the economically weaker sections of society.

The scheme aims to enhance the income levels of families living below the poverty line by promoting livestock farming.

The specific target is to establish at least 5,000 piggery units and 10,000 sheep and goat units across Haryana by the end of the financial year 2023-2024.

The benefits of the scheme include financial assistance for setting up piggery, sheep, and goat units.

Under this scheme, beneficiaries can receive a subsidy of up to 50 percent of the total project cost.

For piggery units, the maximum financial assistance is capped at INR 1 lakh per unit.

For sheep and goat units, the maximum financial assistance is capped at INR 75,000 per unit.

The scheme also provides training and technical support to beneficiaries to ensure successful livestock management.

Eligibility criteria for this scheme require applicants to be residents of Haryana.

Applicants must belong to families classified as Below Poverty Line (BPL).

The age limit for applicants is set between 18 and 55 years.

Educational qualifications are not a strict requirement, but basic literacy is encouraged for effective management of the units.

The application process involves several steps.

Interested applicants must first obtain the application form from the local Animal Husbandry Department office or download it from the official Haryana government website.

The completed application form must be submitted along with required documents.

Required documents include proof of residence, BPL certificate, identity proof, and any relevant educational certificates.

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the local Animal Husbandry Department officials.

The officials will conduct a field visit to verify the information provided in the application.

If approved, beneficiaries will receive a sanction letter detailing the financial assistance.

Disbursement of funds is typically made in two installments.

The first installment is released upon approval of the project.

The second installment is released after the successful establishment of the unit and verification by officials.

The scheme is designed to be implemented by the Animal Husbandry Department of Haryana.

Contact details for the Animal Husbandry Department can be found on the official Haryana government website.

The department provides helpline numbers and email addresses for queries related to the scheme.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to promote self-employment and entrepreneurship among rural households.

It aligns with the government's goal of doubling farmers' income by 2022.

The scheme also contributes to improving the nutritional status of families by promoting livestock farming.

The livestock sector is a significant contributor to the rural economy in Haryana.

The state government has allocated a budget of INR 50 crores for the implementation of this scheme in the financial year 2021-2022.

The scheme also encourages women to participate in livestock farming, promoting gender equality in rural employment.

Training programs are organized regularly to educate beneficiaries about best practices in animal husbandry.

These training sessions cover topics such as animal health management, feeding practices, and marketing strategies.

The scheme is expected to create direct employment opportunities for around 30,000 individuals in the state.

In addition to direct employment, the scheme also aims to create indirect employment opportunities in related sectors.

This includes feed production, veterinary services, and marketing of livestock products.

The government is also working on creating a market linkage for the products generated from these units.

This will help beneficiaries sell their products at fair prices and ensure a steady income.

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries who have successfully established their units.

Many beneficiaries have reported an increase in their household income as a result of this initiative.

The government is continuously monitoring the progress of the scheme to ensure its effective implementation.

Regular assessments are conducted to evaluate the impact of the scheme on beneficiaries' livelihoods.

The scheme is part of the Mukhya Mantri Antyodaya Parivaar Utthan Yojana, which aims to uplift the poorest families in Haryana.

This overarching scheme includes various components aimed at providing financial assistance and skill development.

The government is committed to enhancing the living standards of marginalized sections of society through such initiatives.

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of sustainable agricultural practices.

By promoting livestock farming, the government aims to reduce dependency on traditional crop farming.

This diversification is crucial for enhancing resilience against climate change and market fluctuations.

The scheme is expected to play a vital role in achieving food security in the state.

Overall, the Scheme for Providing Employment Opportunities by Establishing Piggery, Sheep and Goat Units (General) is a significant step towards empowering rural households in Haryana.

It provides a structured approach to improving livelihoods through livestock farming.

The scheme not only addresses unemployment but also contributes to the overall economic development of the state.

The government encourages eligible families to take advantage of this scheme to improve their economic conditions.

By establishing livestock units, families can secure a sustainable source of income and improve their quality of life.

This initiative is a testament to the Haryana government's commitment to poverty alleviation and rural development.

In conclusion, the scheme represents a comprehensive effort to uplift the economically disadvantaged sections of society through targeted support and empowerment.
